page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8252C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at an all-core turbo frequency of up to 4.5 GHz, paired with 192 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz (4.0 GB per vCPU). As a bare-metal deployment, it offers direct access to underlying hardware without hypervisor overhead, including hardware virtualization flags (VMX) and AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. It incorporates 100 Gbps baseline networking throughput, contains no integrated local storage, and includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate pronounced strengths in memory subsystem performance and high-frequency execution. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved top-tier results in PassMark memory throughput, supported by strong large-block uncached read speeds of 235.79 GB/s and write speeds of 97.89 GB/s. High core frequencies yield top-quartile execution in single-threaded gzip compression and Clang software compilation benchmarks. General integer and floating-point benchmarks, such as multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests, perform within the median range. LLM text generation rates remain low, illustrating the expected limits of CPU-only execution for generative machine learning tasks.

Resource efficiency on m5zn.metal centers on its high clock speed and full hardware access combined with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Because local NVMe storage is omitted, overall deployment costs require accounting for network-attached storage via Amazon EBS. The balance of 100 Gbps networking and dedicated compute capacity favors throughput-demanding applications that require bare-metal predictability.

This server type is suitable for high-throughput software compilation, CI/CD runners, network-intensive workloads, gaming backends, in-memory caching systems, and general-purpose enterprise application suites that benefit from high single-core frequencies and physical hardware access.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server offering dedicated access to an Intel Xeon 8252C x86_64 processor. The configuration delivers 24 physical cores, 48 vCPUs running at up to 4.5 GHz, and 192 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It features 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled local storage, and no discrete GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, m5zn.metal registers top-tier PassMark memory scores and top-quartile throughput in large-block uncached memory operations and Clang compilation tasks, while multi-core compute and database operations perform around median baseline levels. Lacking onboard disks, persistence is handled through network-attached storage. This hardware setup is well suited for build pipelines, CI/CD systems, network-heavy application servers, and enterprise software demanding high clock speeds and bare-metal hypervisor avoidance.
